title: The text kitchen
story: The pizzeria's ordering system is full of text: prices to display, scribbled order slips to read, and a chat filter for the delivery drivers, who keep typing things that scare the customers. Build a module of text and maths tools to handle all of it.
create: A ModuleScript named `TextTools` inside `Test07`, returning a table of functions.

requirements.text: It returns a table with the functions `formatPrice`, `initials`, `parseOrder`, `censor`, `roundTo` and `clampSpeed`.
`formatPrice(amount)` returns a dollar sign and the amount with exactly two decimal places, like `"$12.50"` or `"$3.00"`.
`initials(fullName)` returns the first letter of every word, in capitals, with no spaces: `"Mary Ann Hill"` gives `"MAH"`. Extra spaces anywhere are ignored, and an empty name gives `""`.

`parseOrder(text)` reads slips shaped exactly like `"3x pepperoni"`: a whole number, an `x`, at least one space, then the item. It returns the count as a number and the item as a string, like `3, "pepperoni"`. For anything not in that shape it returns `nil`.

`censor(message, badWords)` returns the message with every exact, case-sensitive occurrence of each word in the `badWords` array replaced by the same number of asterisks. Words may contain characters like dots, which must be treated as plain text.
`roundTo(value, places)` returns the value rounded to that many decimal places, with halves rounding away from zero: `roundTo(3.14159, 2)` is `3.14`.
`clampSpeed(speed)` returns the speed kept between 0 and 32.

hints: formatPrice is one call to string.format. initials loops over the words with gmatch.
For parseOrder, write one anchored pattern with two captures, then convert the number capture with tonumber before returning it.
In censor, the word is plain text but gsub expects a pattern. Escape every non-alphanumeric character in the word with a percent sign first, then build the asterisks with rep.

static.fail: Create a ModuleScript named `TextTools` inside the `Test07` folder.

check:
local path = "ServerScriptService.Course.Test07.TextTools"
local T, info = Course.load(path)
local ok = type(T) == "table"
Course.check("r2", ok, "TextTools should return a table of functions, but it returned " .. Course.show(T) .. (if info.error then " (" .. info.error .. ")" else ""))
local names = { "formatPrice", "initials", "parseOrder", "censor", "roundTo", "clampSpeed" }
if ok then
	for _, name in names do
		Course.check("r2", type(T[name]) == "function", "TextTools." .. name .. " should be a function, but it's " .. Course.show(T[name]) .. ".")
	end
end

local function try(id, name, args, compare, wanted)
	if not ok or type(T[name]) ~= "function" then
		Course.fail(id, "Not checked: TextTools." .. name .. " is missing.")
		return
	end
	local results = table.pack(Course.call(T[name], table.unpack(args, 1, args.n or #args)))
	local shown = {}
	for i = 1, (args.n or #args) do
		shown[i] = Course.show(args[i])
	end
	local label = name .. "(" .. table.concat(shown, ", ") .. ")"
	if not results[1] then
		Course.fail(id, label .. " errored: " .. tostring(results[2]))
		return
	end
	local got = { table.unpack(results, 2, results.n) }
	local shownWanted = if type(wanted) == "string" then wanted else Course.show(wanted)
	Course.check(id, compare(got, wanted), label .. " should return " .. shownWanted .. ", but returned " .. Course.show(got))
end
local function same(got, wanted)
	if #got ~= #wanted then
		return false
	end
	for i = 1, #wanted do
		if got[i] ~= wanted[i] then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end
local function close(got, wanted)
	return #got == 1 and type(got[1]) == "number" and Course.near(got[1], wanted[1], 1e-9)
end

for _, case in { { 12.5, "$12.50" }, { 3, "$3.00" }, { 0.1 + 0.2, "$0.30" }, { 1234.567, "$1234.57" }, { 0, "$0.00" } } do
	try("r3", "formatPrice", { case[1] }, same, { case[2] })
end
for _, case in { { "Mary Ann Hill", "MAH" }, { "bob vance", "BV" }, { "  ghost   driver  ", "GD" }, { "", "" }, { "x", "X" } } do
	try("r4", "initials", { case[1] }, same, { case[2] })
end
for _, case in { { "3x pepperoni", { 3, "pepperoni" } }, { "12x ghost chilli", { 12, "ghost chilli" } }, { "pepperoni", {} }, { "x3 cheese", {} }, { "2x", {} }, { "7x  garlic bread", { 7, "garlic bread" } }, { "abc 3x pepperoni", {} }, { "3xpepperoni", {} } } do
	local wanted = case[2]
	try("r5", "parseOrder", { case[1] }, function(got)
		if #wanted == 0 then
			return got[1] == nil
		end
		return got[1] == wanted[1] and got[2] == wanted[2]
	end, if #wanted == 0 then "nil" else wanted)
end
for _, case in {
	{ "the monster is here", { "monster" }, "the ******* is here" },
	{ "run run RUN", { "run" }, "*** *** RUN" },
	{ "a ghost and a goblin", { "ghost", "goblin" }, "a ***** and a ******" },
	{ "all clear", {}, "all clear" },
	{ "price 3.50 now", { "3.50" }, "price **** now" },
	{ "price 3750 and 3.50", { "3.50" }, "price 3750 and ****" },
} do
	try("r6", "censor", { case[1], case[2] }, same, { case[3] })
end
for _, case in { { 3.14159, 2, 3.14 }, { 2.5, 0, 3 }, { 1234.5678, 1, 1234.6 }, { -1.25, 1, -1.3 }, { 7, 3, 7 } } do
	try("r7", "roundTo", { case[1], case[2] }, close, { case[3] })
end
for _, case in { { 10, 10 }, { -5, 0 }, { 40, 32 }, { 32, 32 }, { 0, 0 } } do
	try("r8", "clampSpeed", { case[1] }, same, { case[2] })
end
steps: In the `TextTools` tab, make a module table with these six functions, and return it at the end.
`formatPrice(amount)`: `formatPrice(12.5)` gives `"$12.50"`, and `formatPrice(3)` gives `"$3.00"`. Always two decimal places.
`initials(fullName)`: the first letter of every word, in capitals. `initials("Mary Ann Hill")` gives `"MAH"`. Extra spaces don't matter, and an empty name gives `""`.

`parseOrder(text)`: `parseOrder("3x pepperoni")` gives two values, the number `3` and the string `"pepperoni"`. Anything not shaped exactly like that, such as `"pepperoni"`, `"3xpepperoni"` or `"abc 3x cheese"`, gives `nil`.

`censor(message, badWords)`: replaces each bad word with the same number of stars. `censor("the monster is here", {"monster"})` gives `"the ******* is here"`. Capitals must match exactly, and a dot in a bad word means a real dot, not "any character".
`clampSpeed(speed)`: keeps the speed between 0 and 32 using `math.clamp`. So `clampSpeed(40)` gives `32`, and `clampSpeed(-5)` gives `0`.
